thread:
sara: Quick sync — thinking through a lift-and-shift networking plan for customers moving from hosted -> VPC/private. Goal: minimize IP churn + customer downtime. I'm sketching three paths: direct peering (customer BGP/peering), nat-relay (relay in customer's DMZ), overlay proxy (app-level proxy + mTLS). Need tradeoffs, launch gates, and a minimal installer change set. Who can help risk-assess?

mike: I can take peering tradeoffs. Quick note: direct peering gives best latency but ops burden on both sides. Also SLA edge cases if customer's router flaps. :warning:

anika: nat-relay seems attractive for customers behind strict NATs — less network config on their side but we have to run relay nodes in customer zone or allow egress to our relay. Privacy/logging implications.

raj: overlay proxy reduces L3 complexity; mostly an application-level change. But it's new code path for us — requires KV cache handling and session affinity in the proxy. Performance risk.

lena: Installer impact — we need one small flag and a handshake flow. Proposed minimal installer change: `--network-mode=[peering|relay|overlay]` and a post-install `redwood-net handshake --mode relay --cidr 10.0.0.0/24`. That's the least invasive.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Scheduled maintenance window template created: `priv-net-migration-window-v1` (see /ops/templates).

mike: Launch gates I care about: 1) automated rollback path, 2) observable SLOs for latency and token success rate, 3) documented runbook for customer netops.

anika: Also add KMS/HSM integration check for relay mode — don't want tokens egressing unencrypted. Need cert/rotation checklist.

raj: For canarying: recommend tenant-scoped canaries with prefix caching enabled. If overlay proxy, test with short sequences (<=128 tokens) then ramp to 1k+ sequences.

sara: Good. Drafting acceptance criteria so we can converge:
- Minimal installer changes (single flag + handshake CLI)
- Customer-managed BGP peering doc + config templates for top 3 clouds
- Relay option documented with dataflow diagram and privacy checklist
- Overlay proxy prototype performance within 20% of hosted baseline for p50 latency
- Rollback: traffic split + auto-fallback to hosted API if any SLO breach >2m
- Telemetry: token-level latency + cache hit rate + success ratio visible in Console
- Security: KMS integration verified, cert rotation automated, audit logs enabled

lena: Can we add an offline preflight that validates IP overlap and port ACLs? I can add `preflight --check-ip-collisions` to the installer.

mike: Also include a cost estimate per option (eg relay infra cost, egress cost for peering, dev effort for overlay). We should present it to PMs.

anika: Customer communications: draft email + migration checklist. Include recommended maintenance window length (2h for peering, 45m for relay, 30m for overlay).

raj: Risk matrix idea: columns = [impact, likelihood, detection], rows = [peering, relay, overlay]. I'll sketch it and share.

sara: Awesome. Action items: @mike peering risk doc by EOD, @raj risk matrix + canary plan by tomorrow noon, @lena add preflight check PR, @anika privacy/KMS checklist + comms draft. I'll collate and propose launch gating metrics.

mike: ack :thumbsup:

anika: on it.

lena: PR opened: https://git.redwood/repo/installer/pull/142 — adds `--network-mode` and preflight hooks.

raj: Uploaded initial risk matrix: https://paper.redwood/risk/priv-net-lift-and-shift (comments welcome).

sara: Thanks all. We'll review in the sprint planning slot Friday at 11. If anyone can't make it, drop notes here. :calendar:
